name: WENO3-JS (r = 2), finite-difference flux form
source: Jiang and Shu, J. Comput. Phys. 126 (1996), r = 2: candidates from Table 1, C_k = 1/3, 2/3 (Table 2), IS_k = (f[j+k-1, 1])^2 (2.19); critical points: Henrick, Aslam and Powers (2005), Table 10

claims.why: f' != 0: beta_0, beta_1 = (f' dx)^2 (1 -+ (f''/f') dx + ...), omega_k = d_k + O(dx), but uniformly in the centre, so the difference keeps order 3 (Jiang and Shu p. 7, 'in most smooth regions')
the linear part already has a non-zero dx^3 term
convex weights of second-order candidates: O(dx^2)/dx
at the i-1/2 stencil the leading betas are (9/4, 1/4) f''^2 dx^4, the limit weights are not d_k; Henrick et al. Table 10 gives rate 1
eps fixed: beta = O(dx^4) << eps, weights d_k + O(dx^4)
